MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 16, 2018

 A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
 order at 7:00 p.m. in the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
 Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

 2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

 3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Romanelli, Giglia, Persichina, Pope, Portugal
  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Wroan, Retz
  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Mike Whitehead, Administrative Services Director
  Heidi Luce, City Clerk

 4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 19, 2018
  COMMISSIONER POPE moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA
  TO APPROVE THE CORRECTED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MARCH 19, 2018
  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so moved.

 5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

 7.  BUSINESS ITEMS
  C.  ACTION ITEM FROM CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING OF APRIL 11,
  2018 (Taken out of order)
  Community Services Director Clark reported that representatives from the Park and Activities
  Commission, the Equestrian Committee, Betty’s Foundation, and the Empty Saddle Club attended
  the City Celebration Subcommittee meeting where a discussion was held and it was decided that
  a recommendation be made by the Park and Activities Commission to the City Council to approve
  the 2018 City Celebration be held at Ernie Howlett Park in collaboration with the Remember the
  Music Festival.

  COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL stated that emphasis was placed on having a more collaborative
  effort in coordinating the event.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there was discussion on trying to minimize overlap
  in entertainment with exception of the pony rides and petting zoo and also to hold a shorter event
  with the booths remaining open for the rest of the day.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA asked if there was discussion about having a hay ride at the park. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that he would need to check the logistics - some of the area may be
  too narrow. Following brief discussion, it was noted that the park area is not conducive to having a
  hay ride

  Carrie Silvano, 4709 Rockbluff Place, expressed concerns with the City Celebration being held at
  Ernie Howlett Park and suggested that it be held at the Empty Saddle Club. Ms. Silvano stated
  that she feels that the event has not been successful and no longer embraces the heritage of the
  city and stated that she and another resident donated items in an attempt to draw more people to
  the festival and it did not work. Ms. Silvano stated that the City Celebration should go back to its
  roots and embrace the city.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  1
COMMISSION MINUTES
APRIL 16, 2018
   VICE CHAIR GIGLIA stated that the City Celebration should be inclusive of all the demographics
  in the city and holding the event at Ernie Howlett Park provides an opportunity to include all
  components of the city. He stated that the Empty Saddle Club is exclusively equestrian.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that there were things in the first two events at Ernie Howlett Park that
  could be improved and recommended that residents attend future meetings to provide input in
  planning the event.

  Rich Oldroyd, 40 Ranchview, thanked Carrie and Vicki for their volunteer work. Mr. Oldroyd stated
  that going forward the city should work towards enhancing the equestrian image of the city.

  Vicki Shinn, 23 Roanwood, expressed concern with the logistics of the equestrians getting to Ernie
  Howlett Park and also added that she does not understand the need to hold the entire event at one
  location. Ms. Shin suggested that the equestrian portion be held at the Empty Saddle Club and
  the music festival remain at Ernie Howlett Park on the same day. Ms. Shin stated that the
  equestrian representation at the City Celebration subcommittee meeting feel that the event should
  return to the original venue, but would like to keep an open mind and work with the city. Ms. Shinn
  read a letter from Sean Martin, 2 Empty Saddle Road, who expressed similar concerns.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA stated that there was discussion at the subcommittee meeting on improving
  accessibility and accommodations for the equestrians including making more room for trailers. This
  year there will be no other events scheduled during the equestrian shows and the emcee will
  announce when they are going on. COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL stated that there was discussion
  on the need to be more inclusive and reflective of the equestrian community.

  Karah Woesner, Betty’s Foundation, stated that last year they raised $13K in support of
  Alzheimer’s disease Research. The initial intent of the collaboration with the city was to have the
  music festival after the City Celebration to provide entertainment for a longer period of time and
  keep people at the event. Ms. Woesner stated that last year was their first year collaborating with
  the city and also wanted to clarify that they too embrace the country feel of the community. She
  stated that she would like to collaborate with the city and in no way are they intending to take over
  the event with the music festival.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that due to the various angles of this event, there needs to be a
  compromise in order to make things work. Suggestions have been made to address the concerns
  of the equestrians and it is important that all involved work together.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL to,

  RECOMMEND THAT CITY COUNCIL APPROVE HOLDING THE 2018 CITY
  CELEBRATION EVENT AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK IN COLLABORATION WITH THE
  REMEMBER THE MUSIC FESTIVAL.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  A.  COMMISSIONER IPADS DISTRIBUTION AND TRAINING (Training Session by
  Administrative Services Director)

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead stated that the purpose for the iPads is so that the
  Commissioners can access iLegislate, a product of Granicus, which will eliminate the need for
  paper agendas.

  Tom Pulls, Out of the Box I.T., provided additional information and training.

  B.  ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES HOA ENTRYWAY LANDSCAPING
  MODIFICATIONS

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary on this item.

  Susie Seamans, Rolling Hills Country Club Estates HOA, provided an update on the modifications
  to the Rolling Hills Country Club Estates entryway landscaping and signs. The main portion is
  redoing the pilasters and signs and stated that the HOA decided that the sign will only have
  “Welcome to Rolling Hills Country Club Estates”. Ms. Seamans stated that the HOA is requesting
  an additional sign on the East side of Narbonne Avenue to highlight Club View Lane which is the
  entry into the neighborhood. Ms. Seamans stated that the HOA may decide to use the existing
  pilasters since cost is an issue.

  In response to a question from VICE CHAIR GIGLIA, Ms. Seamans stated that the signs for Club

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  2
COMMISSION MINUTES
APRIL 16, 2018
   View Lane will be the typical white background with green reflective lettering.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA asked if the amount awarded for this project last year is still available.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that it is still earmarked for this project.

  In response to a question from CHAIR ROMANELLI, Ms. Seamans stated that the HOA is
  requesting the removal of two Carrotwood trees and would like to replace it with California oak trees
  and is part of this proposal.

  Ms. Seamans stated that the city’s policy of a $2,500 stipend should be reviewed for HOA’s that
  require this amount of work.

  COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL stated that the concern is approval of the redesign of the monument
  signs.

  Ms. Seamans further suggested that the City’s policy on paying for the city street signs (white with
  green letters) should be changed as well. Community Services Director Clark stated that the city’s
  policy is that if an HOA requests a city street sign, it is paid by the HOA.

  The Commission thanked Ms. Seamans for the update on the project.

  D.  ACTION ITEM FROM PARK AND DESIGN DEVELOPMENT CONSULTANT SELECTION
  SUBCOMMMITTEE INTERVIEW OF APRIL 4, 2018

  Community Services Director Clark provided a summary of the staff report and stated that that
  Commissioner’s Pope, Romanelli, and Retz met with BMLA Landscape who have a sub-component
  for small projects.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the recommendation is that the Park and Activities
  Commission recommend to the City Council to enter into an agreement for the design and
  development of a quarter acre park at the northeast corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos
  Verdes Drive East with BMLA Landscape Architects.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the meeting with the consultants was good and they will be able to
  handle this project, however, he would like to know when the total cost of the project will be
  determined as the proposal only includes the consultant portion. Community Services Director
  stated that it will be determined when there is a conceptual design.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA asked if the proposed amount will get the project to the point of a conceptual
  design and pricing. Community Services Director stated that it does and decisions can be made on
  the features in the park.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE,

  TO RECOMMEND THAT CITY COUNCIL ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH BMLA
  LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURE FOR THE DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF A ¼-ACRE
  PARK ON THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  F.  POCKET PARK DESIGN UPDATE (Taken out of order)

  Community Services Director Clark introduced Andrea Vona, Executive Director, Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) and special guests Mr. and Mrs. Taber, who are making a
  donation to the pocket park project.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief overview of what is being proposed and stated
  that he has concerns with the steps that are being proposed since there was a desire to provide a
  more simple ingress and egress to the location would be to a trail which would be widened and
  improved by the city’s maintenance department. When there is a natural trail into a park there is no
  requirement for ADA access.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA commented that he did not see widening of the equestrian trail. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that there is an intent to widen, improve the surface, and trim any
  trees or shrubs too close to the trail.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that one of the eagle scouts is interested in some projects
  for the park.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  3
COMMISSION MINUTES
APRIL 16, 2018
   Andrea Vona, Executive Director, PVPLC, inquired about 1) the steps to the park in regards to
  maintenance and also if steps are favorable for equestrian use; 2) drainage at the site; and 3) if the
  trail shown on the conceptual plan is consistent with the existing trail. Community Services Director
  stated that the intent is to keep the bridle trail as it is with improvements.

  Mr. Taber state that it seems the project is going in the right direction. (Video not audible for
  additional comments made by Mr. Taber).

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA asked about the property adjacent to the nature center. Community Services
  Director Clark stated that this should be part of the discussion and will look into it.

  The Park and Activities Commission thanked Mr. Taber for attending the meeting and for his
  generous donation.

  E.  PARKS AND FACILITIES NAMING POLICY

  Community Services Director Clark stated that at the City Council’s Policy Development session
  there was a suggestion made that when naming a facility after a community member that it be done
  during the lifetime of a person rather than after they pass. He noted that in researching the matter,
  staff found an existing naming policy which has been updated to reflect that suggestion.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI inquired about the reason for changing the policy at this time. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that he does not know the reason.

  COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL, seconded by VICE CHAIR GIGLIA,

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE CIT CITY COUNCIL ADOPT THE REVISED CITY
  PROPERTY AND FACILITIES NAMING POLICY

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  G.  MONTECILLO HOA LANDSCAPE SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark reported on the Montecillo HOA Landscape Subcommittee
  meeting. In attendance were VICE CHAIR GIGLIA, CHAIR ROMANELLI, and COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that it was a good meeting and recommendations were made.
  Members of the HOA were present to discuss the Cal Water project process.

  CHAIR GIGLIA stated that HOA is metering their work with the Cal Water project.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that they have made significant improvements to the
  median landscaping. Catalina Cherry shrubs will be planted and removal of buried concrete aprons
  has been completed.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  Community Services Director Clark thanked CHAIR ROMANELLI for pointing out the leaking
  drinking fountain and stated that the maintenance crew has fixed the problem.

  VICE CHAIR GIGLIA stated that the water faucets on the outside of the barn are leaking.

  9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  PARK DESIGN CONSULTANT SELECTION UPDATE (See item 7D)

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 27, 2018

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 10, 2018

  C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 26, 2018

  COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA,

   TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 10-A THROUGH 10-C

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there have been internal reorganization and Jessica
  Slawson is now Administrative Analyst. She will now be handling emergency preparedness for the
  city. Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager, will be contacting the Area G representative to
  come and speak at a future meeting.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:35 p.m. VICE CHAIR GIGLIA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PORTUGAL,

  TO ADJOURN TO AN ADJOURNED MEETING THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION AT 6:00 P.M. ON MAY 21, 2018 AT 27305 PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST
  FOR THE PURPOSE OF CONDUCTING A PARK TOUR OF GEORGE F. CANYON
  NATURE CENTER, DAPPLEGRAY PARK AND THE NEW POCKET PARK.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  The next Park and Activities Meeting will be held on Monday, May 21, 2018 at 6:00 p.m. at George
  F. Canyon Nature Center, Dapplegray Park, and the new pocket park.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk
